extracted.intended_audience: senior biomedical researchers (faculty-level) seeking HHMI Investigator appointment or institutions hosting such investigators
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions and standards used by the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) to select and support HHMI Investigators, including program philosophy, researcher qualities, appointment terms, and special award criteria (e.g., plant-science partnership and Collaborative Innovation Awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: People, not projects selection philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our philosophy of selecting “people, not projects” seeks researchers who bring innovative approaches to the study of many different biological problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI funds individuals rather than specific project grants, giving long-term flexible support so investigators can pursue ideas even if directions change; selection focuses on the person’s potential to make significant contributions rather than a single proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity and productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI investigators are widely known for their creativity and productivity and are pushing the bounds of knowledge in biomedical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track record of creative, high-impact work is valued; the current group includes Nobel laureates and NAS members, indicating expectation of exceptional accomplishment and influence in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to take risks and tolerate failure
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI urges its researchers to take risks, explore unproven avenues, and embrace the unknown—even if it means uncertainty or the chance of failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI’s long-term, flexible funding model is intended to allow investigators to pursue high-risk, high-reward ideas without immediate project-level constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on significant biological questions pursued rigorously and deeply
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators identify and pursue significant biological questions in a rigorous and deep manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate a history or plan of addressing important biological problems with depth and rigor rather than superficial or incremental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological and technical innovation (develop new tools/methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators develop new tools and methods that enable creative experimental approaches to biological questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI values investigators who create enabling technologies or inventive approaches, including adoption or adaptation of techniques from other disciplines, to open new lines of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary approaches / bring concepts from other disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: When necessary bringing to bear concepts or techniques from other disciplines (e.g., biophysics, chemical biology, biomedical engineering, computational biology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-disciplinary thinking that expands experimental capability or conceptual framing is encouraged; HHMI looks for investigators who integrate methods or ideas across fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking basic biology and medicine (translational potential)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators forge links between basic biology and medicine, opening new pathways for disease diagnosis and drug discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that creates clear opportunities to impact human health or enable translational advances is an important valued dimension, though HHMI supports a broad range of basic and adjacent fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of eligible scientific disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI seeks investigators across many biomedical disciplines (genetics, cell biology, developmental biology, biochemistry, neuroscience) and adjacent fields (biophysics, chemical biology, biomedical engineering, computational biology); plant scientists, evolutionary biologists, and patient-oriented researchers are also included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is intentionally broad in disciplinary scope; applicants from diverse biological and adjacent quantitative/engineering disciplines are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host-institution partnership and continued institutional engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI investigators are based at host institutions across the United States and continue to participate in educational and administrative activities at their host institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection assumes and requires collaborative partnerships with host institutions; investigators remain engaged in institutional responsibilities while receiving HHMI support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment terms and review for renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment is for a five-year term, which may be renewed after an exacting review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators are selected through periodic competitions and must undergo rigorous evaluation at renewal to continue HHMI appointment beyond the initial five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment and financial support model
rubrics_metrics.description: By employing scientists as investigators rather than awarding grants for specific research projects, HHMI provides investigators with full salary, benefits, and a research budget; some laboratory personnel may be Institute employees and investigators are supported by HHMI field offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The employment model is designed to give investigators flexibility to change research direction and to follow long-term projects that may take many years to bear fruit.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHMI–Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation (GBMF) investigator criteria (plant sciences)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI-GBMF investigators are creative plant scientists appointed through a partnership with the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation to pursue bold research that could result in large contributions to science and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This targeted partnership seeks to address underfunding in plant sciences by supporting innovative plant biology projects with potential for substantial scientific or societal impact; 14 investigators were appointed to study a variety of plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Innovation Awards (HCIA) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: HCIA support interdisciplinary teams of scientists, each headed by an HHMI investigator, to pursue potentially transformative research projects that are new and so large in scope that they require a team with a range of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HCIA-funded projects are intended to encourage collaboration inside and outside HHMI, enable large-scope, high-risk/high-reward work, provide collaborator research budgets for four years, and offer flexibility; HHMI invited investigators to propose these collaborations and selected awardees after review.
